    Comparing two processing versions of a frame¶

    Frame F08622 (New York City and Long Island), 2016-07 to 2024-12: the same 239 acquisitions processed as product version 1.0 and as 1.1. A new processing version changes the algorithm, not the data, so the two should agree within noise wherever the ground is coherent. This notebook puts them on a common footing (same epochs, same reference) and looks at where they differ: the maps at the last date, the velocities, a few pixel series and the scatter around the reference.

    This notebook ran on real granules; its outputs are saved, and the documentation build does not run it again.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pyproj import Transformer

import disp_xr as dxr

warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
root = Path("/u/operapst/bato/work/CALVAL/disp-s1_official")
versions = {
    name: sorted((root / name / "F08622" / "products").glob("*/*.nc"))
    for name in ("v1.0", "v1.1")
}


def title(ax, text):
    """Title the panel on the left, without xarray's automatic title."""
    ax.set_title("")
    ax.set_title(text, loc="left")


for name, files in versions.items():
    table = dxr.find_products(files)
    print(
        f"{name}: {len(table)} granules, {table.reference_time.nunique()} ministacks,"
        f" produced {table.production_time.min():%Y-%m} to"
        f" {table.production_time.max():%Y-%m}"
    )

    Ministacks¶

    Both versions cover the same 239 acquisitions in 16 ministacks. Their reference dates agree except the second: v1.0 starts it on 2017-03-13 and v1.1 on 2016-09-26, so the two chain the first year differently. The table lists the first ministack reference dates of each.

    A common footing¶

    A 30 x 30 km window over Brooklyn, Queens and lower Manhattan, chained per version, kept to the epochs both have, and referenced to the same 1 km box in Brooklyn.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    west, south, east, north = -74.10, 40.60, -73.75, 40.85
ref_lon, ref_lat = -73.9791, 40.7035
stacks = {}
for name, files in versions.items():
    raw = dxr.open_disp(files, layers=["displacement", "recommended_mask"])
    to_grid = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:4326", raw.rio.crs, always_xy=True)
    (x0, x1), (y0, y1) = to_grid.transform([west, east], [south, north])
    window = raw.sel(x=slice(x0, x1), y=slice(y1, y0))
    stacks[name] = dxr.chain(dxr.mask(window, "recommended"))
common = np.intersect1d(stacks["v1.0"].time.values, stacks["v1.1"].time.values)
box = (ref_lon - 0.005, ref_lat - 0.005, ref_lon + 0.005, ref_lat + 0.005)
for name in stacks:
    stacks[name] = dxr.rereference(stacks[name].sel(time=common), "area", bbox=box)
    stacks[name] = stacks[name].persist()  # read once for the maps, fits and series
print(f"{len(common)} common epochs, {dict(stacks['v1.0'].sizes)}")
    west, south, east, north = -74.10, 40.60, -73.75, 40.85 ref_lon, ref_lat = -73.9791, 40.7035 stacks = {} for name, files in versions.items(): raw = dxr.open_disp(files, layers=["displacement", "recommended_mask"]) to_grid = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:4326", raw.rio.crs, always_xy=True) (x0, x1), (y0, y1) = to_grid.transform([west, east], [south, north]) window = raw.sel(x=slice(x0, x1), y=slice(y1, y0)) stacks[name] = dxr.chain(dxr.mask(window, "recommended")) common = np.intersect1d(stacks["v1.0"].time.values, stacks["v1.1"].time.values) box = (ref_lon - 0.005, ref_lat - 0.005, ref_lon + 0.005, ref_lat + 0.005) for name in stacks: stacks[name] = dxr.rereference(stacks[name].sel(time=common), "area", bbox=box) stacks[name] = stacks[name].persist() # read once for the maps, fits and series print(f"{len(common)} common epochs, {dict(stacks['v1.0'].sizes)}")
    240 common epochs, {'y': 937, 'x': 974, 'time': 240}

    Velocities¶

    MIDAS velocity of each version on the pixels valid in at least half the common epochs in both.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    enough = None
velocity = {}
for name, ds in stacks.items():
    valid = ds.displacement.isel(time=slice(1, None)).notnull().mean("time") >= 0.5
    enough = valid if enough is None else enough & valid
    velocity[name] = 1e3 * dxr.fit_velocity(ds, method="midas").velocity
velocity = {name: v.where(enough).compute() for name, v in velocity.items()}
vdiff = velocity["v1.1"] - velocity["v1.0"]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.6), layout="constrained")
for ax, name in zip(axes[:2], velocity):
    velocity[name].plot.imshow(
        ax=ax, cmap="RdBu", vmin=-5, vmax=5, cbar_kwargs={"label": "mm/yr"}
    )
    title(ax, f"{name} MIDAS velocity")
vdiff.plot.imshow(
    ax=axes[2], cmap="PuOr", vmin=-2, vmax=2, cbar_kwargs={"label": "mm/yr"}
)
title(axes[2], "v1.1 minus v1.0")
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
plt.show()
large = float((abs(vdiff) > 2).sum() / vdiff.notnull().sum())
print(
    f"velocity difference: median {float(vdiff.median()):+.2f} mm/yr,"
    f" 1.4826 MAD {1.4826 * float(abs(vdiff - vdiff.median()).median()):.2f} mm/yr,"
    f" |difference| > 2 mm/yr on {large:.1%} of the pixels"
)
    enough = None velocity = {} for name, ds in stacks.items(): valid = ds.displacement.isel(time=slice(1, None)).notnull().mean("time") >= 0.5 enough = valid if enough is None else enough & valid velocity[name] = 1e3 * dxr.fit_velocity(ds, method="midas").velocity velocity = {name: v.where(enough).compute() for name, v in velocity.items()} vdiff = velocity["v1.1"] - velocity["v1.0"] fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.6), layout="constrained") for ax, name in zip(axes[:2], velocity): velocity[name].plot.imshow( ax=ax, cmap="RdBu", vmin=-5, vmax=5, cbar_kwargs={"label": "mm/yr"} ) title(ax, f"{name} MIDAS velocity") vdiff.plot.imshow( ax=axes[2], cmap="PuOr", vmin=-2, vmax=2, cbar_kwargs={"label": "mm/yr"} ) title(axes[2], "v1.1 minus v1.0") for ax in axes: ax.set_aspect("equal") plt.show() large = float((abs(vdiff) > 2).sum() / vdiff.notnull().sum()) print( f"velocity difference: median {float(vdiff.median()):+.2f} mm/yr," f" 1.4826 MAD {1.4826 * float(abs(vdiff - vdiff.median()).median()):.2f} mm/yr," f" |difference| > 2 mm/yr on {large:.1%} of the pixels" )
    velocity difference: median -0.01 mm/yr, 1.4826 MAD 0.08 mm/yr, |difference| > 2 mm/yr on 0.2% of the pixels

    Series at four points¶

    The median of a 30 m radius around each point (about one pixel and its neighbors): LaGuardia Airport, lower Manhattan, Woodside and Ridgewood.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    points = {
    "LaGuardia": (-73.871854, 40.771890),
    "Lower Manhattan": (-73.997618, 40.725698),
    "Woodside": (-73.90194, 40.74775),
    "Ridgewood": (-73.91977, 40.71759),
}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 6.5), layout="constrained", sharex=True)
for ax, (label, (lon, lat)) in zip(axes.flat, points.items()):
    x, y = to_grid.transform(lon, lat)
    for name, ds in stacks.items():
        series = 1e3 * ds.displacement.sel(
            x=slice(x - 30, x + 30), y=slice(y + 30, y - 30)
        ).median(("y", "x"))
        ax.plot(series.time, series, ".-", ms=2, lw=0.6, label=name)
    ax.set(title=label, ylabel="mm")
axes[0, 0].legend()
plt.show()
    points = { "LaGuardia": (-73.871854, 40.771890), "Lower Manhattan": (-73.997618, 40.725698), "Woodside": (-73.90194, 40.74775), "Ridgewood": (-73.91977, 40.71759), } fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 6.5), layout="constrained", sharex=True) for ax, (label, (lon, lat)) in zip(axes.flat, points.items()): x, y = to_grid.transform(lon, lat) for name, ds in stacks.items(): series = 1e3 * ds.displacement.sel( x=slice(x - 30, x + 30), y=slice(y + 30, y - 30) ).median(("y", "x")) ax.plot(series.time, series, ".-", ms=2, lw=0.6, label=name) ax.set(title=label, ylabel="mm") axes[0, 0].legend() plt.show()

    Scatter around the reference¶

    With the reference box assumed stable, the spread of the pixels within 1 km of it, epoch by epoch, is a direct look at each version's noise at short distance.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    x, y = to_grid.transform(ref_lon, ref_lat)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 3.6), layout="constrained")
for name, ds in stacks.items():
    near = 1e3 * ds.displacement.sel(
        x=slice(x - 1000, x + 1000), y=slice(y + 1000, y - 1000)
    )
    spread = near.std(("y", "x")).compute()
    ax.plot(
        spread.time,
        spread,
        ".-",
        ms=2,
        lw=0.6,
        label=f"{name}: median {float(spread.median()):.1f} mm",
    )
ax.set(ylabel="std within 1 km of the reference (mm)")
ax.legend(loc="upper left")
plt.show()
    x, y = to_grid.transform(ref_lon, ref_lat) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 3.6), layout="constrained") for name, ds in stacks.items(): near = 1e3 * ds.displacement.sel( x=slice(x - 1000, x + 1000), y=slice(y + 1000, y - 1000) ) spread = near.std(("y", "x")).compute() ax.plot( spread.time, spread, ".-", ms=2, lw=0.6, label=f"{name}: median {float(spread.median()):.1f} mm", ) ax.set(ylabel="std within 1 km of the reference (mm)") ax.legend(loc="upper left") plt.show()

    What changed¶

    • Where the ground is coherent, the two versions agree within their noise.
      • At the last date, on the 66% of pixels valid in both: a median difference of -0.2 mm, spread 0.4 mm (1.4826 MAD).
      • In velocity: a median difference of -0.01 mm/yr, spread 0.08 mm/yr. Only 0.2% of the pixels differ by more than 2 mm/yr, isolated pixels scattered across the window.
    • LaGuardia Airport is the one point of the four where the series part: from about 2019, v1.1 sits a few millimetres above v1.0.
    • v1.1 is quieter near the reference. The pixel spread within 1 km of it has a median of 5.1 mm, against 5.6 mm for v1.0, and is lower at almost every epoch.
